text:
alice (AE): FYI — Acme POC load test is hitting 429s after ~10k concurrent requests. They're blocked on validation tests. Also they just sent the security questionnaire Q1 about request-log retention. Need swarming.
ben (SE): Can you drop a sample request-id and which cluster/route? I want to check gateway metrics.
alice (AE): request-id: rq_20240321_acme_07, route: /v1/generate -> edge-us-west-2 -> customer id ACME-42. Error visible in their logs: 429 rate_limited. Example snippet from their side:
```
2024-03-21T15:21:34Z [edge] req=rq_20240321_acme_07 status=429 reason=rate_limited route=/v1/generate
```
charlie (SRE): I can see matching entries on our gateway. Rate-limiter token_bucket exhausted for key ACME-42, burst window hit. 429s are from our token bucket, not upstream. Investigating if they hit global QPS or per-key.
dana (eng-runtime): Are calls all using the same API key? If yes, we can temporarily raise per-customer throttle or route them to a dedicated pool. Also can enable short prefix caching to reduce token churn. Can you confirm headers (x-api-key / x-customer-id)?
alice (AE): Yes same API key. Header sample they attached: `x-customer-id: ACME-42`, `x-api-key: live-xxxx`. They want to continue tests ASAP — need workaround while we triage.
emma (security): On the retention Q: defaults are 30 days for request logs, encrypted at rest, access audited. We can produce a redacted sample and SOC2 attestation PDF. If they need custom retention we have an enterprise option.
ben (SE): @charlie can we temporarily bump ACME-42 to 200 rps for the POC? Need ETA to make change and how to revert.
charlie (SRE): I can apply a safe override in the rate-limit config for that customer. ETA ~15 minutes. Will also add a fallback route to a model-variant-cpu if GPU pool is under pressure, so they don't get 429s from capacity pressure.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rate-limiter-override ACME-42 -> 200rps by charlie at 2024-03-21T15:36Z
dana (eng-runtime): I'll also push a small runtime change: prefix cache TTL 5s + logging of token_bucket_fill_rate for the next 1h to gather metrics. Rollback safe.
alice (AE): Quick billing question from customer: will this bump get charged extra? They want a sense before we do it.
ben (SE): Bursts are billed at the on-demand unit rate; if they sustain we should propose a short-term Dedicated commit or negotiated POC pricing. I'll loop in finance after we confirm duration.
charlie (SRE): Override applied at 15:36 UTC. Monitoring dashboard: 429s dropping, 200s/3xx steady. I'll keep the override for 30 minutes and watch for anomalies. If stable, we can let them run for the rest of their tests.
alice (AE): Customer says their tests resumed, initial pass looks good :thumbsup: — asking for confirmation we sent the security docs.
emma (security): Sent redacted logs + SOC2 PDF to acme-security@acme.com and updated the questionnaire with our answers. I'll follow up on any clarifications.
dana (eng-runtime): Root-cause notes: gateway backpressure + aggressive per-key throttle. Opening internal task RINF-7321 to improve header-aware backpressure and add a safer fallback path. Will include an eval of moving short-lived bursts to a separate burst token bucket.
charlie (SRE): Leaving override in place for 30m, will close when counts are stable for 15m. Created ticket INF-SUP-1029 referencing acct ACME-42 and the request-id. Assigning to eng-runtime for the follow-up.
alice (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll update the ACME stakeholders and schedule a short post-mortem with them tomorrow. Marking as in-progress until SRE closes INF-SUP-1029.
ben (SE): Noted — I'll prepare a one-pager for possible POC pricing if they need sustained capacity.
alice (AE): Customer confirmed completion of their validation tests. Please keep the ticket open for the post-mortem and close after the follow-up task is created. Much appreciated :clap:
